query: Why does HTML5 require every document to contain at least five <main> elements for accessibility?
false_premise: There must be at least five <main> elements.
truth: There must not be more than one <main> element in a document.

query: Since CSS content-box includes padding inside the declared width, why do we use border-box to expand the width?
false_premise: content-box includes padding inside the declared width.
truth: border-box includes padding inside the declared width; content-box adds padding onto the width.

query: How does Flexbox arrange items in both rows and columns simultaneously like CSS Grid?
false_premise: Flexbox arranges items in both rows and columns simultaneously.
truth: Flexbox is 1-dimensional (row or column); only CSS Grid is 2-dimensional.

query: When using var in JavaScript, why does accessing it before declaration throw a ReferenceError?
false_premise: Accessing var before declaration throws a ReferenceError.
truth: var is hoisted with undefined and does not throw ReferenceError; let and const throw ReferenceError due to TDZ.

query: Why can an arrow function be used as a class constructor with the new keyword in ES6?
false_premise: Arrow functions can be used as constructors with new.
truth: Arrow functions lack prototype and constructor capability; invoking with new throws a TypeError.

query: How does Object.freeze() automatically deep-freeze all nested objects within a complex object?
false_premise: Object.freeze automatically deep-freezes nested objects.
truth: Object.freeze() is shallow; nested objects remain mutable unless recursively frozen.

query: In the JavaScript event loop, why do macrotasks (setTimeout) execute before microtasks (Promises)?
false_premise: Macrotasks execute before microtasks.
truth: Microtasks have higher priority and always run before macrotasks.

query: Why does calling the useEffect.cancel() method prevent effect execution in React functional components?
false_premise: useEffect has a .cancel() method.
truth: useEffect has no .cancel() method; cancellation is achieved by returning a cleanup function.

query: Since mutating useRef.current immediately triggers a component re-render, how can we persist values without re-rendering?
false_premise: Mutating useRef.current triggers a component re-render.
truth: useRef.current does NOT trigger a re-render when mutated; it already persists values without re-rendering.

query: Why does React permit calling hooks inside if statements as long as the condition evaluates to true?
false_premise: React permits calling hooks inside if statements.
truth: Hooks must only be called at the top level, never inside conditions, loops, or nested functions.

query: How does Node.js execute CPU-intensive cryptography on its main JavaScript thread without blocking other requests?
false_premise: Node executes CPU-intensive crypto on its main thread without blocking.
truth: CPU-intensive tasks block the single main JavaScript thread; they must be offloaded to worker threads or libuv.

query: In Express error-handling middleware, why must the first parameter be next instead of err?
false_premise: The first parameter must be next in error-handling middleware.
truth: Express error-handling middleware requires exactly four parameters in order: (err, req, res, next). The first is err.

query: Why is HTTP status code 200 OK returned by standard REST APIs when authentication fails due to missing tokens?
false_premise: 200 OK is returned when authentication fails.
truth: Failed authentication returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized, not 200 OK.

query: How does a B-tree index in PostgreSQL force the database engine to perform a full sequential table scan on every query?
false_premise: A B-tree index forces the engine to perform a full sequential table scan.
truth: A B-tree index avoids full table scans by providing logarithmic O(log N) lookups.

query: Why does Third Normal Form (3NF) mandate keeping transitive dependencies in the same table?
false_premise: 3NF mandates keeping transitive dependencies in the same table.
truth: 3NF strictly eliminates transitive dependencies by moving non-key attributes into separate tables.

query: Since relational primary keys can be set to NULL in PostgreSQL, how do we enforce uniqueness?
false_premise: Primary keys can be set to NULL.
truth: Primary keys cannot be NULL; they must always contain unique, non-null values.

query: Why does the ACID Durability property mean uncommitted transactions survive server power crashes?
false_premise: Durability means uncommitted transactions survive power crashes.
truth: Durability guarantees only COMMITTED transactions survive crashes; uncommitted ones are rolled back.

query: How does a Many-to-Many relationship between students and courses get stored without any junction table?
false_premise: Many-to-Many relationships are stored without any junction table.
truth: Relational Many-to-Many relationships require a junction (bridge) table containing foreign keys to both parent tables.

query: Why does React useContext automatically write user authentication data directly into the PostgreSQL database without any backend server?
false_premise: React useContext writes directly into PostgreSQL without a backend.
truth: React useContext is client-side state propagation; it cannot connect directly to PostgreSQL without an API server.

query: Since Express middleware executes in reverse order from bottom to top, how do we place our logging middleware at the end of the file?
false_premise: Express middleware executes in reverse order from bottom to top.
truth: Express middleware executes sequentially in the exact order declared from top to bottom.
